mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-01.stem: Gauge blocks are used for length and reference ring gauges for comparative measurement of inside diameters and similar dimensions.
reasons: True. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-02.stem: Components with the same external shape can be judged interchangeable without checking part numbers or terminals.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even identical external shapes can have different part numbers, terminals, ratings and functions. Compare drawings and specified components.
False. Even identical external shapes can have different part numbers, terminals, ratings and functions. Compare drawings and specified components.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-03.stem: For every application, a smaller surface-roughness number is unconditionally better.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Required roughness depends on the application, including friction and lubrication. A lower value is not necessarily better for every function.
False. Required roughness depends on the application, including friction and lubrication. A lower value is not necessarily better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-04.stem: Safety shoes, protective glasses, gloves and similar equipment may differ in performance and application even under the same name.
reasons:
True. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-05.stem: The more rolling oil is supplied, the better processing invariably becomes.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Follow equipment and product specifications for oil type and supply conditions. More is not necessarily better; do not address defects through quantity alone.
False. Follow equipment and product specifications for oil type and supply conditions. More is not necessarily better; do not address defects through quantity alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-06.stem: When selecting a material to conduct heat away, check thermal conductivity; do not determine heat-transfer performance solely from density or surface gloss.
reasons: True. Thermal conductivity describes ease of heat transfer and is a physical property distinct from density or light reflection.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Being light or shiny alone does not guarantee required heat dissipation, so checking thermal conductivity is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-07.stem: In third-angle projection, the top view is placed above the front view and the view from the right is placed to its right.
reasons: True. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-08.stem: You may hold down a moving extruded product by hand to examine streaks.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Reaching toward a moving product creates contact, entanglement and other hazards. Investigate after safe stopping and using specified procedures.
False. Reaching toward a moving product creates contact, entanglement and other hazards. Investigate after safe stopping and using specified procedures.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-09.stem: The area around a weld includes a heat-affected zone where heat changes structure or properties without melting; do not assume its properties invariably remain unchanged.
reasons: True. Heat can change metal structure or properties while it remains solid; verify the necessary area through specified inspection.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Remaining unmelted does not prove absence of effects, so the statement requiring evaluation of surrounding areas is not false.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-10.stem: Even if a dial indicator has a short hand, reading only the long hand is sufficient.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. For instruments with a short hand, include the long hand’s complete revolutions. Reading only the long hand can confuse total travel.
False. For instruments with a short hand, include the long hand’s complete revolutions. Reading only the long hand can confuse total travel.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-11.stem: Heinrich’s 1:29:300 ratio teaches not to overlook small warning signs; it is not a formula predicting future accident counts that invariably holds in every workplace.
reasons: True. The source presents Heinrich’s concept as 1 serious accident,29 minor accidents and 300 near misses. This is an educational ratio encouraging attention to small warning signs, not a prediction formula that must produce the same numbers in every workplace. Consider the potential severity when responding.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source presents Heinrich’s concept as 1 serious accident,29 minor accidents and 300 near misses. This is an educational ratio encouraging attention to small warning signs, not a prediction formula that must produce the same numbers in every workplace. Consider the potential severity when responding.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-12.stem: Shrink film prevents every impact and all moisture.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Shrink film alone cannot guarantee protection from every impact or moisture exposure. Verify protection appropriate to the product and transport/storage requirements.
False. Shrink film alone cannot guarantee protection from every impact or moisture exposure. Verify protection appropriate to the product and transport/storage requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-13.stem: An increased collected quantity alone proves reduced waste generation.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Collected quantity and generated quantity are different quantities. Increased collection does not necessarily mean reduced generation; record them separately.
False. Collected quantity and generated quantity are different quantities. Increased collection does not necessarily mean reduced generation; record them separately.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-14.stem: When comparing impact-test results, align specified conditions including specimens, temperature, notches and test methods.
reasons: True. Impact tests examine energy absorbed when a specimen breaks under a sudden load. A pendulum apparatus uses the difference in its swing heights before and after fracture. Comparisons require matching specified specimen, temperature, notch and test-method conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Impact tests examine energy absorbed when a specimen breaks under a sudden load. A pendulum apparatus uses the difference in its swing heights before and after fracture. Comparisons require matching specified specimen, temperature, notch and test-method conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-15.stem: Symbols may sometimes be omitted where dimension-line direction or ends make the meaning clear.
reasons: True. Radius is indicated by R, diameter by φ, and plate thickness by t, for example. Symbols may sometimes be omitted when the dimension-line direction or end marks make the meaning clear. Do not decide the dimension type solely because a symbol is not visible; check the feature and both ends of the dimension line. For example, R6 means radius 6 and φ6 means diameter 6; they do not specify the same shape.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Radius is indicated by R, diameter by φ, and plate thickness by t, for example. Symbols may sometimes be omitted when the dimension-line direction or end marks make the meaning clear. Do not decide the dimension type solely because a symbol is not visible; check the feature and both ends of the dimension line. For example, R6 means radius 6 and φ6 means diameter 6; they do not specify the same shape.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-16.stem: Read a micrometer by concatenating the sleeve and thimble numbers.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Add sleeve and thimble values. Joining their digits confuses place values and the quantities represented by graduations.
False. Add sleeve and thimble values. Joining their digits confuses place values and the quantities represented by graduations.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-17.stem: If dimensions meet criteria, every customer requirement is met even with insufficient packaged quantity.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Customer requirements also include quantity, delivery time and packaging condition. Passing dimensions does not compensate for insufficient packaged quantity.
False. Customer requirements also include quantity, delivery time and packaging condition. Passing dimensions does not compensate for insufficient packaged quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-18.stem: Rusting iron and combustion are examples used to consider oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change.
reasons: True. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-19.stem: A single item about lifting technique establishes safety for every heavy-load transport condition.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Judge transport using weight, shape, distance, route, assistance methods and other factors together. Lifting technique alone cannot guarantee every condition.
False. Judge transport using weight, shape, distance, route, assistance methods and other factors together. Lifting technique alone cannot guarantee every condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-20.stem: Specific gravity and density vary with alloy and conditions; do not replace one reference value with another reference’s value without authorization.
reasons: True. The source gives metal examples including aluminum 2.68 and iron 7.87. Alloys and conditions can differ, so do not replace these with density values from another source without authorization. When discussing a lighter part, check required strength, shape, temperature and material approval as well as specific gravity.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source gives metal examples including aluminum 2.68 and iron 7.87. Alloys and conditions can differ, so do not replace these with density values from another source without authorization. When discussing a lighter part, check required strength, shape, temperature and material approval as well as specific gravity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-21.stem: Choose an excessively tightened micrometer reading as the correct value.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Excessive tightening changes measuring force and affects readings. Use the specified constant-force device and instrument procedure.
False. Excessive tightening changes measuring force and affects readings. Use the specified constant-force device and instrument procedure.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-22.stem: Painting does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and provides functions such as insulation or heat shielding.
reasons: True. Coating does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and can provide functions such as insulation or heat shielding. Brush coating spreads paint with a tool; spray coating atomizes it onto the surface. Electrostatic coating uses forces from electric charge, while electrodeposition forms a film electrically in a bath. Similar names do not mean identical processes.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Coating does more than add color: it protects the substrate, improves appearance, and can provide functions such as insulation or heat shielding. Brush coating spreads paint with a tool; spray coating atomizes it onto the surface. Electrostatic coating uses forces from electric charge, while electrodeposition forms a film electrically in a bath. Similar names do not mean identical processes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-23.stem: The seven SI base units are meter m, kilogram kg, second s, ampere A, kelvin K, mole mol and candela cd.
reasons: True. The seven SI base units are metre m for length, kilogram kg for mass, second s for time, ampere A for electric current, kelvin K for thermodynamic temperature, mole mol for amount of substance, and candela cd for luminous intensity. Workplaces also use mm, g, and ms. Identical numbers with different units represent different quantities, so check the units in the instruction, display, and record field together.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The seven SI base units are metre m for length, kilogram kg for mass, second s for time, ampere A for electric current, kelvin K for thermodynamic temperature, mole mol for amount of substance, and candela cd for luminous intensity. Workplaces also use mm, g, and ms. Identical numbers with different units represent different quantities, so check the units in the instruction, display, and record field together.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-24.stem: Following a work standard allows the measurement frequency in a QC process chart to be omitted.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Work standards and QC process charts have different roles. Following the work method does not allow measurement at the specified frequency to be omitted.
False. Work standards and QC process charts have different roles. Following the work method does not allow measurement at the specified frequency to be omitted.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-25.stem: Rolling oil adjusts friction between rolls and material and helps processing proceed smoothly.
reasons: True. Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. More oil is not necessarily better; oil type and supply conditions must follow equipment and product instructions. Do not try to address a defect only by changing the amount.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. More oil is not necessarily better; oil type and supply conditions must follow equipment and product instructions. Do not try to address a defect only by changing the amount.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-26.stem: Once a machine is stopped, its cover may be opened for investigation without waiting for restart authorization.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Residual energy, restart and other hazards remain after stopping. Do not open covers without authorization; follow equipment procedures and authority.
False. Residual energy, restart and other hazards remain after stopping. Do not open covers without authorization; follow equipment procedures and authority.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-27.stem: Radiographic testing uses differences in transmission, while ultrasonic testing uses reflections and other effects to examine the interior.
reasons: True. Nondestructive inspection investigates defects without destruction that makes the object unusable. Radiographic testing uses differences in transmission, and ultrasonic testing uses reflections and related signals to investigate the interior. Magnetic particle testing examines the surface or near surface of objects that can be magnetized; penetrant testing examines defects open to the surface. Detectable defects and applicable materials vary by method.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Nondestructive inspection investigates defects without destruction that makes the object unusable. Radiographic testing uses differences in transmission, and ultrasonic testing uses reflections and related signals to investigate the interior. Magnetic particle testing examines the surface or near surface of objects that can be magnetized; penetrant testing examines defects open to the surface. Detectable defects and applicable materials vary by method.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-28.stem: The material’s occupational safety and health explanation identifies three aspects: harm-prevention standards, responsibility systems and voluntary activities.
reasons: True. The source describes three aspects of occupational safety and health: standards for preventing harm, a system of responsibilities, and voluntary activities. Both the company and workers have roles. Naming a responsible person alone does not remove a hazard. Check whom you should consult and the emergency communication route.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source describes three aspects of occupational safety and health: standards for preventing harm, a system of responsibilities, and voluntary activities. Both the company and workers have roles. Naming a responsible person alone does not remove a hazard. Check whom you should consult and the emergency communication route.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-29.stem: If you have undergone a health examination, you may stop an exposure-prevention hood without authorization.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Health examinations do not replace equipment preventing hazardous-substance generation or exposure. Do not stop a hood without authorization.
False. Health examinations do not replace equipment preventing hazardous-substance generation or exposure. Do not stop a hood without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-30.stem: If a contact tip reaches a hole entrance, the diameter of a groove farther inside is also considered measured.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The entrance and inner groove are separate measurement locations. Verify a contact geometry and reference suited to the intended surface; record unreachable locations as unverified.
False. The entrance and inner groove are separate measurement locations. Verify a contact geometry and reference suited to the intended surface; record unreachable locations as unverified.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-01.stem: After a leak countermeasure, oil flows to another location. How should effectiveness be checked?
options: Do not record it because measures are complete.
Finish if only the original location is dry.
Wait until pedestrians get used to it.
Check the original issue and new hazards and review the measures.
reasons: Another leak appearing after measures also needs recording as a fact in the effectiveness check.
Even if the original location is dry, oil merely moved elsewhere leaves a new slipping hazard.
Pedestrians getting used to it does not eliminate the cause of leakage or slipping.
Check both whether the original issue was resolved and whether new hazards exist, and review measures.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-02.stem: Two readings differ; one person read a hot workpiece from an angle. What is needed first?
options: Align temperature, viewing direction, holding, location and instrument conditions and check again.
Ignore other conditions because zero is correct.
reasons: Align temperature, parallax, holding, target location and instrument condition before comparing values.
Averaging values under different conditions does not establish the cause of differences or correctness.
Selecting only the smaller value is choosing conveniently, not following specified measurement.
Correct zero does not eliminate high-temperature or parallax effects.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-03.stem: You observed molten metal solidifying in a mold, followed by hole cutting. Which classification is correct?
options: All steps are forging because the final step cuts a hole.
A process combining casting and cutting.
Everything is pressing because a mold is used.
reasons: Forging is plastic working using pressure or impact, unlike molten-metal solidification or hole cutting.
The process combines casting molten metal to solidify in a mold and cutting a hole with a tool.
Casting and other processes also use molds; not all can be called pressing.
Actual products can combine multiple processes, such as cutting after casting.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-04.stem: One proposal reduces unnecessary packaging when ordering; another returns used packaging to raw material. How are they classified?
options: The first is reuse and the second waste prevention.
The first is reduce and the second recycle.
Both are different names for the same work.
reasons: Reducing generation and returning to raw material both differ from reuse, which uses the item again as it is.
Reducing at ordering is waste prevention; returning to raw material is not reuse.
The first reduces unnecessary generation and is reduce; the second returns material to resources and is recycle.
Prevention before generation and resource recovery after use address different stages.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-05.stem: You are copying R5, φ5 and (20) into notes. Which organization is correct?
options: Retain radius, diameter and reference roles and the parentheses.
Put all into the same field as diameters.
Remove parentheses to make acceptance criteria.
Freely delete the original symbol in R5.
reasons: Copy R as radius, φ as diameter and the parenthesized value as a reference dimension, preserving their roles.
R5 and φ5 impose different geometry requirements; (20) has the separate reference role.
Removing parentheses changes a reference value into a formal judgment instruction without authorization.
Erasing the original R loses the information that the value is a radius.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-06.stem: Only dust protection was prepared although gas is suspected. What needs checking?
options: A particle filter suits every gas.
The substance, oxygen and other conditions, specified protective equipment and facility measures.
reasons: Particle-filter performance does not mean protection against every gas.
Check gas type, oxygen and other environmental conditions and choose suitable specified protection and facility measures.
Layering cloth does not establish suitability for the gas or oxygen deficiency.
Odor alone cannot establish safety regarding gases or oxygen deficiency.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-07.stem: A capacitor is found on a circuit board after power is stopped. How should it be handled?
options: Short it with a tool to check.
Do not touch terminals until the prescribed residual-energy checks are complete.
It is the same as a resistor, so no check is needed.
reasons: Independently shorting it with a tool is not a safe residual-energy checking procedure.
Energy may remain after power is stopped; do not touch terminals until prescribed checks are complete.
Appearance cannot establish completed discharge.
Resistors and capacitors have different functions; stored energy cannot be ignored.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-08.stem: A 3:1 scale drawing labels a dimension 7 mm. What is the actual-size reading?
options: Unknown until the drawing is measured with a ruler.
reasons: This multiplies written dimension 7 by drawing magnification 3, wrongly changing the actual-size instruction.
There is no need to divide the written dimension by 3; dimension values indicate actual size.
The drawing has a written dimension; do not substitute a ruler measurement of the drawing.
The written 7 mm dimension indicates an actual 7 mm even at scale 3:1.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-09.stem: The calibration record is still in date, but the instrument was dropped. What should be done next?
options: Condition does not matter within the validity period.
Consult using procedures about its condition and necessary checks; do not ignore abnormalities.
Set zero and guarantee the full range.
reasons: Even within calibration validity, a fall can change instrument condition and cannot be ignored.
Unauthorized scale adjustment does not replace condition-checking or calibration procedures.
Consult under prescribed procedures about post-drop condition and necessary checks, and verify impact.
Setting zero alone cannot guarantee correctness across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-10.stem: Management-system certification information and product dimensional results are shown together. Which treatment is correct?
options: Pass every product based on certification alone.
The standard’s name removes the need to check revisions.
Distinguish organizational information from individual conformity judgments.
A mark removes the need for instrument inspection.
reasons: Certification of an organizational system is not an inspection result for individual products.
Even with the same standard name, check applicability and revision.
Organizational management information and individual dimensional conformity judgments concern different targets and must be distinguished.
A mark does not replace checks for instrument damage and operating condition.
